listBibl.bibl: Felix Liebermann, Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen, vol. 1 (Halle: Niemeyer, 1903), p. 520

An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.ab: Cuncta ergo diuina simul et humana eius nutum expectabant; quæ cuncta ut paucis animaduertantur, quædam de iis quæ noua per Angliam seruari constituit ponam, æstimans illa scitu esse necessaria ad cognitionem eorum quorum causa maxime istud scribendi onus suscepimus:
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 520 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: All things, therefore, divine and human alike, awaited his nod; and so that all of them may be perceived in a few words, I shall set down some of those things which he decreed should be observed as new throughout England, judging them necessary to be known for the understanding of those things for whose sake above all we have taken up this burden of writing:
